I'm rating a few character story arcs best to worst according to my opinion. These are TV ratings, I haven't read the books and any content in them isn't being included.

 

Best - Tyrion Lannister

Seeing Tyrion go from (apparently) spoiled Lannister to black sheep of the family, to having his whore betray him and murdering his father, crossing the sea and becoming an administrator of a powerful warlord. Tyrion has never had a dull moment. He's experienced every emotion that an actor is capable of portraying. If I were going to give a story arc 10/10, it would be Tyrion's

 

Runner Up - Theon Greyjoy

Theon's always been in a hard spot as far as his character growth goes. Although he didn't immediately appear to be an important character, every moment that he was on the screen was defining parts of his personality. His change from before and after imprisonment is almost realistic, and his motivations and desires are so human that he's easy to identify with. Going into the next season, I expect for Theon to have a lot of changes and action.

 

Least Best - John Snow

John has had incredible growth over the series. We've seen him go from the bastard to the ruler of Winterfell. He's had love, he's lost, he's met death. He has clearly defined values based on his experiences and he has become a main character, from someone we might have expected to die early on. The only slow parts of his story are, when at the wall, the white walkers are still yet undiscovered. There is a bit there where not much happens, but it work well because its the calm before the storm; the enemy that he's been fighting against (one of many) is coming to its full power.

 

Second Worst - Arya Stark

Arya was a seemingly unimportant character for much of the series. Although she's had a few shining moments, e.g. her time with The Hound, she spends a lot of time going in circles. In Bravos especially, her story is completely disrupted when, instead of training and growing into an assassin as her history indicated she would, she performs inhuman feats and slays someone who'd been kicking her butt for the last season. Her new talents are cool, but it feels less like a story and more like a fantastic dream.

 

Worst - Daenerys Targaryen

Unfortunately for Danny, the writers got ahead of George R.R. Martin and decided to have her fart around for a long while without getting a lot done, much like Arya. Although her introduction and rise were very interesting, the boredom that sets in when she's ruling Mereen and trying to hunt down the Son's of the Harpies is too much. Way too much air time was devoted to those events and it made the story feel really stagnant. It picks up when the slavers decide to attack, and hopefully, moving forward, she isn't plagued by such relentless nothings.

 

If an arc hasn't been included, it hasn't been rated and isn't necessarily better or worse than any of the other arcs.
